Trace-one generators make the contact cone closed. Strict separation, a small negative scalar shape correction, and uniform support control inside and outside a contact neighborhood contradict maximality. The cone dimension gives d+d(d+1)/2 contacts, and the trace gives total weight d.

The direction A^{-1}v supports the contact c+Av. Mixing the original dominated laws with weights λ/d keeps mass and base mean, and the between-source covariance contributes only A²/d in the continuous block. The within-source blocks remain in the full covariance.

At strict mass, a finite supergradient of the raw support along the balanced mass line exists. The prescribed-slope theorem applies at the supported raw moment t(c+Av), giving an actual finite cap. For a common source density factor one can divide the entire raw graph by that factor, apply the same support plane with unchanged slope, and scale back.

Each normalized hinge integrates to t(u·c+1−b). Continuous balance cancels u·c, and testing the aggregate positive part on an attained mass-T balanced source gives −BT without any sign assumption on B. Rearrangement gives B≥−dt/(T−t) and the claimed upper bound.

For identical unit intervals the balanced fills are upper and lower intervals of length t/M on every fiber. The radius is (M−t)/(2M), so each hinge integral is t²/(M−t), with ratio t/M to the upper bound.
